de29_precedent.topic: Domestic surveillance precedent 1945-1975 and modern query abuses

claims.text: Operation CHAOS grew from a Special Operations Group set up in August 1967 and was terminated 15 March 1974; its computer index held about 300,000 names of persons and organisations, most American; about 7,200 personality files on US citizens and nearly 1,000 organisation files.

Rockefeller Commission: 'Some domestic activities of Operation CHAOS unlawfully exceeded the CIA's statutory authority', though the declared mission of gathering intelligence abroad on foreign influence was proper; 'Two Presidents and their staffs made continuing and insistent requests'; CIA's own 1969 and 1970 assessments found no evidence of foreign control of the movements.

MINARET: NSA watch list of 1,650 US citizens whose overseas calls and cables were monitored; named targets included Sen. Frank Church (D-Idaho), Sen. Howard Baker (R-Tenn.), Tom Wicker, Art Buchwald, Martin Luther King Jr., Whitney Young and Muhammad Ali; NSA historian Thomas Johnson wrote it was 'disreputable if not outright illegal'.

The material came from NSA history 'American Cryptology during the Cold War' via National Security Archive FOIA and ISCAP appeal after ~8 years; GW Today quotes 'disreputable if not downright illegal' and gives 1961-1973 (dating disputed).

SHAMROCK: Western Union, RCA and ITT gave NSA copies of international telegrams; at peak ~150,000 messages a month analysed; Church called it 'probably the largest government interception program affecting Americans ever undertaken'; NSA director Lew Allen ended it in May 1975 as Congress began investigating.

Media, Pennsylvania FBI office burgled 8 March 1971; files revealed spying on left and liberal groups and first reference to COINTELPRO; Betty Medsger of the Washington Post first published; John and Bonnie Raines and Keith Forsyth named in 2014; never charged, FBI closed case 11 March 1976 after the statute of limitations ran.

COINTELPRO began 1956 (CPUSA), then SWP 1961, KKK/white hate groups 1964, Black nationalist 1967, New Left 1968; officially terminated April 1971; Church Committee called it a 'sophisticated vigilante operation'; anonymous package to King 21 November 1964.

Laird v. Tatum (26 June 1972, 5-4, Burger): Army system was 'the collection of information about public activities'; allegations of subjective chill 'are not an adequate substitute for a claim of specific present objective harm'; no justiciable controversy.

IRS Special Service Staff (by 1969 to mid-1973) targeted about 8,000 individuals and 3,000 groups for political activity, using FBI and DOJ lists; included the Ford Foundation and the Urban League; dissolved in mid-1973 by commissioner Donald Alexander.

Stellar Wind: 2009 joint IG report released to NYT via FOIA in April 2015; a 2004 FBI review found only 1.2 percent of tips 2001-04 made a 'significant contribution'; none of the content tips Aug 2004-Jan 2006 useful; March 2004 hospital-room confrontation of Comey and Goldsmith.

FISC opinion released 19 May 2023: FBI improperly queried 702 data on more than 100 people arrested at June 2020 racial-justice protests, on 6 January suspects, and in a batch of about 19,000 donors to a congressional campaign (DOJ: only eight identifiers had sufficient foreign ties); compliance rose from 82% to 96% after reforms per FBI audit.
